traceability.evidence:
Implementation file src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts: - Rule uses hardcoded patterns: - Story path pattern: const pathPattern = /^docs\/stories\/[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-DEV-[\w-]+\.story\.md$/; - Requirement ID pattern: const reqPattern = /^REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+$/; - Rule meta schema does not accept any options: meta: { ..., schema: [], fixable: "code", } - create(context) does not read context.options or any configuration fields such as storyPathPattern, requirementIdPattern, storyPathExample, or requirementIdExample. - Error message helpers (buildStoryErrorMessage, buildReqErrorMessage) use only hardcoded examples: - STORY_EXAMPLE_PATH = "docs/stories/005.0-DEV-EXAMPLE.story.md"; - Messages always reference these fixed examples and cannot be customized. - No references to docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md or to requirements REQ-PATTERN-CONFIG, REQ-REGEX-VALIDATION, REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT, REQ-EXAMPLE-MESSAGES, REQ-SCHEMA-VALIDATION, REQ-CONSISTENCY, or REQ-PATTERN-TESTING appear in this rule.
Comparison rule src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts (used in story’s guidance for consistency): - Defines a JSON schema with configurable options (storyDirectories, allowAbsolutePaths, requireStoryExtension). - Reads options from context.options[0] and applies defaults, demonstrating the project’s pattern for configurable rule options that 010.1 expects valid-annotation-format to follow. valid-annotation-format has not been updated to match this pattern.
Tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts: - Cover only default, hardcoded behavior: - Valid/invalid @story paths using docs/stories/... .story.md. - Valid/invalid @req IDs matching ^REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+$. - No tests configure the rule with storyPathPattern, requirementIdPattern, storyPathExample, or requirementIdExample. - No tests for invalid regex patterns in configuration or configuration-time validation failures. - No tests verifying that custom example strings appear in error messages. - Test header and describe blocks only reference stories 005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION and 007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING; there is no mention of 010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.
Documentation in docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md: - Describes only fixed patterns: - Story paths must match ^docs/stories/[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-DEV-[\w-]+\.story\.md$. - Requirement IDs must match ^REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+$. - No documentation of rule options storyPathPattern, requirementIdPattern, storyPathExample, or requirementIdExample. - No examples of custom pattern configuration as shown in the story (e.g., prompts/..., custom requirement prefixes, specifications/... formats).
Story file docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md: - Acceptance criteria checkboxes in the story text are all unchecked. - A repository-wide search shows no code or tests referencing this story file name or its requirement IDs.
traceability.notes: The valid-annotation-format rule has not been extended to support configurable storyPathPattern and requirementIdPattern options. It still relies on hardcoded regexes, defines an empty schema, and does not read any configuration from context.options. Error messages cannot be customized with example strings, and there is no configuration-time regex validation. Tests and documentation only cover and describe the fixed default behavior, with no coverage or examples for the new configuration options. There is no traceability from implementation or tests to story 010.1. Therefore, multiple acceptance criteria (core functionality, backward compatibility via configurable defaults, pattern/regex validation, improved error messages, schema-based validation, consistency with valid-story-reference configuration, and documentation of custom patterns) are not met, so this story is not implemented.
